documents.title: Satyam Computers Services was at the center of a massive $1.6 billion fraud case in 2009 .

facts.statement: Police said an Indian software pioneer and nine others were sentenced to seven years in jail for their roles in what was described as India's biggest corporate scandal in memory.

references.verbatim: An Indian software pioneer and nine others have been sentenced to seven years in jail for their role in what has been dubbed India's biggest corporate scandal in memory, police said.

facts.statement: Ramalinga Raju was the former chairman of Satyam Computers Services.

references.verbatim: Ramalinga Raju, the former chairman of software services exporter Satyam Computers Services, was also fined $804,000, R.K. Gaur, a spokesman for India's Central Bureau of Investigation, told CNN.

facts.statement: A spokesman for India's Central Bureau of Investigation told CNN that Ramalinga Raju was fined $804,000.

facts.statement: In 2009, Satyam Computers Services was at the center of a $1.6 billion fraud case.

references.verbatim: In 2009, Satyam Computers Services was at the center of a massive $1.6 billion fraud case after its then-chairman Raju admitted inflating profits with fictitious assets and nonexistent cash.

facts.statement: Raju admitted inflating profits using fictitious assets and nonexistent cash.

facts.statement: When the scam made headlines, Satyam was India's fourth-largest software services provider.

references.verbatim: When the scam made headlines, Satyam, which means "truth" in Sanskrit, was India's fourth-largest software services provider.

facts.statement: Satyam served almost 700 companies, including 185 Fortune 500 companies.

facts.statement: The Indian government fired Satyam's board after Raju's disclosures.

facts.statement: Satyam was bought by Tech Mahindra in a state-backed auction.

references.verbatim: In a subsequent state-backed auction, the company was bought by Tech Mahindra, part of the country's Mahindra Group.

facts.statement: Raju founded Satyam in 1987.

references.verbatim: He had founded Satyam in 1987.

Fox is developing a two-hour remake of the 1975 cult classic to be directed, executive-produced and choreographed by Kenneth Ortega ("High School Musical").

facts.statement: Kenneth Ortega was slated to direct, executive-produce and choreograph the remake.

facts.statement: Chesterfield High School stopped the payments in 2011.

facts.statement: Judge Daniel Serota ruled that outsiders would consider the payments a "misapplication of public monies."

references.verbatim: In the most recent case, Judge Daniel Serota ruled that outsiders would consider the payments a 'misapplication of public monies ' and that the school was right to stop them.

facts.statement: Anderson had been a senior learning mentor at the school from 2001.

facts.statement: A tribunal ruled that Anderson was not entitled to compensation.

references.verbatim: It also ruled that, while Mr Anderson's belief in public service is a protected status, he had not been discriminated against.
